proposals: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change should validate the user-agency field in PARIVESH and correct existing records, so an individual's name does not appear as the top Forest Clearance user agency with 1,697 proposals and agency-wise counts can be trusted.

MoEFCC should add the date of every status change to the PARIVESH 2.0 open API, so the Forest, Wildlife and CRZ registers can be read as time series showing how long proposals sit at each stage, not only as a single pipeline snapshot.

MoEFCC should publish the rules for PARIVESH auto-delisting and a count of delisted applications by reason, since 11,723 of 28,999 Forest Clearance proposals are delisted and it is not visible how many were abandoned, duplicated or cleaned up for other reasons.

MoEFCC should add range checks on the forest-area field and publish corrections for implausible entries, so a single record of about 74,000 hectares cannot distort the 1.05 million hectare pipeline figure that users of the register will quote.

The National Board for Wildlife's Standing Committee should report, for proposals awaiting wildlife clearance, the time spent pending with the proponent and with the state and national boards separately, so the 4,319 cases in process can be attributed to whoever is actually holding them.
